skills: Draw free-body diagrams for each particle
Apply Newton's second law along the direction of motion
Eliminate tension to find acceleration
Back-substitute to find tension

questions.stem_markdown:
Two particles, of masses 1.8 kg and 1.2 kg, are connected by a light inextensible string that passes over a fixed smooth pulley. The particles hang vertically. The system is released from rest.

Find the magnitude of the acceleration of the particles and find the tension in the string.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: Use of Newton’s second law for either particle or system
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Correct number of terms; allow sign errors. Dimensionally correct.
For any 2 correct equations.
From equations with the correct number of relevant terms. If $$a$$ found first, then substituting into an equation with the correct number of relevant terms and solving.
Both correct.

parts.prompt_markdown: Given that the plane is smooth, use an energy method to find the speed of the particle at B.

It is given instead that the plane is rough and the particle reaches B with a speed of 8 m s$^{-1}$. The plane is 25 m long and the constant frictional force has magnitude F N.

Find the value of F.

assets.description: Right-triangle incline diagram with points A, B and C. The vertical drop from A to B is labelled 12.5 m, and the right angle is at C.

skills: Use conservation of energy on a smooth surface
Equate gravitational potential energy change to kinetic energy plus work by forces
Apply energy/work equation with friction to find the friction force

questions.stem_markdown: A particle of mass 7.5 kg, starting from rest at A, slides down an inclined plane AB. The point B is 12.5 metres vertically below the level of A, as shown in the diagram.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Either correct.

$$5\sqrt{10}$$. **SC B1** for $$v^2 = 0^2 + 2(g \sin \theta) \left( \frac{12.5}{\sin \theta} \right) \Rightarrow v = 15.8$$ (or with cos). **B0** for $$v^2 = 0^2 + 2g \times 12.5 \Rightarrow v = 15.8$$ or correct answer with no working.
Attempt at work energy equation; 3 terms; dimensionally correct; allow sign errors.
Finding the correct acceleration down the plane.
Newton’s second law parallel to the plane; allow sign errors and sin/cos mix on the weight component; dimensionally correct. Allow with their $$a$$, or just $$a$$.

assets.description: Mechanics force diagram showing perpendicular forces of 52 N and 39 N with the resultant force P N making angle $\theta$.

relationships: $\theta$ is the angle shown in the diagram

skills: Use equilibrium conditions
Set up simultaneous component equations
Solve for unknown force magnitude and angle
methods: Resolve forces into x and y components

questions.stem_markdown:
Coplanar forces of magnitudes 52 N, 39 N and P N act at a point in the directions shown in the diagram. The system is in equilibrium.

Find the values of P and $\theta$.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: Resolving in any direction to get an equation
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Allow sin/cos mix. only – or for $$P^2 = 39^2 + 52^2$$ or $$\tan \theta = \frac{52}{39}$$. (allow reciprocal for M mark).
Both correct – or for both $$P^2 = 39^2 + 52^2$$ and $$\tan \theta = \frac{52}{39}$$.
Attempt to solve for either $$P$$ or $$\theta$$ from equations with the correct number of relevant terms. OE using sin/cos with $$P$$
Both correct; 53.13010…

parts.prompt_markdown: Sketch the velocity-time graph for the bus's journey from A to B.
Find an expression, in terms of $a$, for the length of time that the bus is travelling with constant speed.
Given that the distance from A to B is 3000 m, find the value of $a$.

assets.description: Blank velocity-time graph axes for sketching, labelled $t$ (s) and $v$ (m s$^{-1}$).

skills: Sketch a velocity-time graph from acceleration phases
Use constant-acceleration kinematics to express time intervals
Combine distances over phases to solve for an acceleration parameter
methods: Use v = u + at and s = ut + 1/2 at^2

questions.stem_markdown: A bus travels between two stops, A and B. The bus starts from rest at A and accelerates at a constant rate of $a\,\text{m s}^{-2}$ until it reaches a speed of $16\,\text{m s}^{-1}$. It then travels at this constant speed before decelerating at a constant rate of $0.75a\,\text{m s}^{-2}$, coming to rest at B. The total time for the journey is 240 s.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Correct shape, starting at $$O$$ and finishing on the $$t$$-axis.
Attempt at finding either the time for accelerating or for decelerating – must be in terms of $$a$$.
OE – allow un-simplified.
Use distance is area under the graph.

Get an expression in terms of $$a$$ ONLY using their $$T$$ from part (b) and solve for $$a$$ – their $$T$$ must have come from an expression of the form $$240 - \frac{k_1}{a} - \frac{k_2}{a}$$ where $$k_1$$ and $$k_2$$ are positive constants. OE e.g. $$3000 = 16 \times 240 - \frac{1}{2} \times 16 \times \frac{16}{a} - \frac{1}{2} \times 16 \times \frac{64}{3a}$$.
Allow 0.356 or better.

parts.prompt_markdown: Find the height above O at which the particles collide.
Find the time from A being projected until C returns to O.

skills: Use conservation of momentum to find collision time
Use kinematics to find collision height and subsequent motion

questions.stem_markdown: A particle, A, is projected vertically upwards from a point O with a speed of 80 m s$^{-1}$. One second later a second particle, B, with the same mass as A, is projected vertically upwards from O with a speed of 100 m s$^{-1}$. At time T s after the first particle is projected, the two particles collide and coalesce to form a particle C.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: For use of $$s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$$ at least once with $$a = \pm g$$ and $$u = 80$$ or $$100$$ – allow $$t, T, t \pm 1, T \pm 1$$.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: Two correct expressions for the displacement of both particles at time $$T$$
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Allow $$t$$ for $$T$$.
Equate and attempt to solve for $$T$$ or $$t$$ – must not be using the same time for both expressions (so must be using the equivalent of $$T$$ in one and $$T \pm 1$$ in the other).
**AG** – no errors seen (but allow all working in terms of $$t$$).
OR $$100 \times 2.5 - \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 2.5^2$$.

For use of $$v = u + at$$ at least once to find the speed at collision with $$a = \pm g$$, $$u = 80$$ or $$100 -$$ with $$t = 2.5$$ or $$3.5$$ only (but condone $$2.5$$ with $$v_A$$ and $$3.5$$ with $$v_B$$).
Use of conservation of momentum, 3 non-zero terms, allow sign errors. If total momentum before collision not correct then it must be clear where both terms came from.
Complete method to find an equation in $$t$$ using their $$v$$, their height from part **(b)** and $$\pm g$$ - dependent on both previous M marks.

assets.description: Mechanics diagram of a particle of mass 1.2 kg on an inclined rough plane at angle $\theta$, with the normal reaction shown. The question refers to a horizontal force $P$ acting in the plane of the diagram.

relationships: Particle is on an inclined plane
Normal reaction is perpendicular to the plane
A horizontal force acts in a vertical plane containing the line of greatest slope

skills: Resolve forces parallel and perpendicular to the plane
Use limiting friction condition
Set up equilibrium equations to find the least possible P
subtopics: Force resolution with horizontal force direction constraints

questions.stem_markdown:
A particle of mass 1.2 kg is placed on a rough plane which is inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\theta = \frac{3}{25}$. The particle is kept in equilibrium by a horizontal force of magnitude P N acting in a vertical plane containing a line of greatest slope (see diagram). The coefficient of friction between the particle and the plane is 0.15.

Find the least possible value of P.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: Attempt at resolving perpendicular to the plane to get an equation
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Correct number of relevant terms, allow sign errors, allow sin/cos mix, allow g missing. For reference $$R = 1.2g \times \cos 16.26\dots + P \times \sin 16.26\dots$$ - allow with an angle of 16 or better.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: Attempt at resolving parallel to the plane to get an equation
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Correct number of relevant terms, allow sign errors, allow sin/cos mix, allow g missing. For reference $$F + P \times \cos 16.26\dots = 1.2g \times \sin 16.26\dots$$ allow with an angle of 16 or better.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: Use of $$F = 0.15R$$ to get an equation in $$P$$ only
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Dependent on both previous M marks – where R is initially a linear combination of a P component and a weight component (or a mass component). $$1.2g \times \frac{7}{25} - P \times \frac{24}{25} = 0.15 \times \left( 1.2g \times \frac{24}{25} + P \times \frac{7}{25} \right)$$.

parts.prompt_markdown: The car travels along a straight level road.

The car has a greatest possible constant speed of $48\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Show that $k = 40$.
At an instant when its speed is $45\text{ m s}^{-1}$, find the greatest possible acceleration of the car.

The car now travels at a constant speed up a hill inclined at an angle of $\sin^{-1}0.15$ to the horizontal.
Find the greatest possible speed of the car going up the hill.

skills: Use maximum power condition to find speed-force relationship
Derive the constant k from the given greatest constant speed
Relate power, resistive force, and net force to acceleration
Apply power to find the greatest possible constant speed up an incline
methods: Newton’s second law with resistive force
subtopics: Power in relation to force and speed

questions.stem_markdown: A car has mass 1200 kg. When the car is travelling at a speed of $v\text{ m s}^{-1}$, there is a resistive force of magnitude $kv\text{ N}$. The maximum power of the car's engine is 92.16 kW.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: For any use of power = $$F_v$$ e.g. $$45 \times DF = 92160$$.
Apply N2L using their $$DF \neq 92160, 92.16, 1920$$. 3 terms; allow sign errors. Dimensionally correct.
Allow 0.207 or better.
Two term expression for the driving force up the hill, allow sign errors and sin/cos mix – dimensionally correct.
Set up an equation in $$v$$ only – must be using $$DF \times v = 92160$$.
Attempt to solve their 3TQ in $$v$$ – dependent on both previous M marks.

skills: Integrate acceleration to obtain velocity as a function of time
Find times when velocity is zero
Integrate velocity to obtain distance between those times

questions.stem_markdown:
A particle P moves in a straight line, passing through a point O with velocity 4.2 m s$^{-1}$. At time t s after P passes O, the acceleration, a m s$^{-2}$, of P is given by $a = 0.6t - 2.7$.

Find the distance P travels between the times at which it is at instantaneous rest.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Attempt to integrate $$a$$ – increase power by 1 and a change in coefficient in at least one term (which must be the same term).
Set up 3TQ in $$t$$ with correct constant term.
Both correct values of $$t$$ (method not required).

Attempt to integrate $$v$$ – increase power by 1 and a change in coefficient in at least one term (which must be the same term) – expression for $$v$$ must be at least two terms (so may not include a constant term) so dependent on first M mark only.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: For use of their positive $$t$$ limits in their cubic expression for $$s$$
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Dependent on all previous M marks. Using their two positive $$t$$ values correctly in their three term cubic expressions for $$s$$ (cubic must contain non-zero $$t^n$$ terms where $$n = 1,2$$ and 3).

For reference: $$(0.1 \times 2^3 - 1.35 \times 2^2 + 4.2 \times 2)$$ $$- (0.1 \times 7^3 - 1.35 \times 7^2 + 4.2 \times 7)$$ If integration of $$v$$ not explicitly shown, then this can score max ***M1 DM1 A1** then **SC B1** for correct answer of 6.25 (so 4 marks max.).
